'''Luis Fernando Alday''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} is an Argentine-British mathematician, and the [[Rouse Ball Professor of Mathematics]] at the [[University of Oxford]] and Head of the Mathematical Physics Group.

== Career ==
Alday was born on 17 October 1977 in [[San Rafael, Mendoza]], but he spent most of his youth in [[Arrecifes]]. He was the eldest child among three siblings.{{Sfn|Iannini|2020}} He graduated from the [[Balseiro Institute]] at the [[National University of Cuyo]] in Argentina in 2001,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Luis Fernando Alday |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1019648 |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> after studying for the first two years at the [[National University of La Plata]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=13 June 2022 |title=Egresado del Balseiro, nuevo integrante de la Royal Society |trans-title=Balseiro Graduate, New Member Of The Royal Society |url=https://www.uncuyo.edu.ar/prensa/egresado-del-balseiro-nuevo-integrante-de-la-royal-society |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=Prensa UNCUYO |language=es}}</ref> He completed his PhD at the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] in [[Trieste]] in 2004. He was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (IAS) in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]] for Spring 2007, and from September 2008 to September 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Kelly Devine |date=2019-12-09 |title=Luis Fernando Alday - Scholars {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/luis-fernando-alday |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=www.ias.edu |language=en}}</ref> At the IAS, he collaborated with [[Juan Maldacena]], a fellow Argentine physicist and Balseiro graduate. Alday joined the [[University of Oxford]] in 2010 after post-doctorate studies at the IAS and [[Utrecht University]]. Since then, he has been associated with [[Hertford College, Oxford|Hertford College]].{{Sfn|Iannini|2020}} His research interests include a bootstrap approach to conformal [[Field theory (physics)|field theories]] and [[string theory]], several aspects of the [[AdS/CFT duality]], four-dimensional N=2 [[Supersymmetric theory of stochastic dynamics|super-symmetric theories]] and their relation to conformal field theories, and the exact computation of [[observable]]s in super-symmetric [[Gauge theory|gauge theories]]. He received a [[Royal Society Wolfson Fellowship]] in 2012, and the [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 2013. Alday has also received two grants from the [[European Research Council]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Luis Fernando Alday {{!}} Mathematical Institute |url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/luis.alday |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=www.maths.ox.ac.uk}}</ref>

Alday's research focuses on providing mathematical tools for applications in areas of physics such as [[quantum field theory]] and [[quantum gravity]]. He was appointed the [[Rouse Ball Professor of Mathematics]] and head of the Mathematical Physics Group in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellow Detail Page {{!}} Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/sitecore/content/royal-society/configuration/foundation/dynamics-api/fellowsdetailpage/ |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=royalsociety.org |language=en}}</ref> Alday was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in May 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-10 |title=Outstanding scientists elected as Fellows and Foreign Members of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2022/05/new-fellows-2022/ |access-date=2022-05-11 |website=Royal Society}}</ref> He was recognised as such for two groundbreaking papers. The first provides a method for computing "[[scattering amplitude]]s in planar super-symmetric [[Yang–Mills theory]] at strong [[Coupling (physics)|coupling]]". The second paper introduced the concept of [[AGT correspondence]], partly named after Alday and developed jointly with [[Davide Gaiotto]] and Yuji Tachikawa, "relates four dimensional supersymmetric gauge theories to two dimensional conformal field theories".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Search Results |url=https://catalogues.royalsociety.org/calmview/Record.aspx?src=CalmView.Catalog&id=EC/2022/01 |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=catalogues.royalsociety.org}}</ref> At the time of his election to the Royal Society, he was a Fellow of [[Wadham College, Oxford|Wadham College]] and associated with the Oxford [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford|Mathematical Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fernando Alday and Alain Goriely elected Fellows of the Royal Society {{!}} Mathematical Institute |url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/60290 |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=www.maths.ox.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Luis Fernando Alday {{!}} Wadham College |url=https://www.wadham.ox.ac.uk/people/luis-fernando-alday |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=www.wadham.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>
